- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in cycle (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently 1.00 (strong bullish), model tends to overfit; cap forecast at 10% below recent 10-day high to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–3% downward adjustment in next 5–7 days.
